newsitem.title: USA: US Airways makes new offer to pilots.
newsitem.headline: US Airways makes new offer to pilots.

text.p: In a move toward reaching a contract agreement with its pilots union, US Airways Group Inc. Thursday offered a guarantee it would expand at a rate comparable to its major competitors.
The offer, which was presented to union negotiators for the first time on Thursday, marked a positive step toward resolving the bitter dispute between the airline and the pilots, labour experts said.
The pilots previously had sought assurance that the airline would grow before it would agree to a new contract.
The proposal came as the union filed a lawsuit against the airline, alleging some of management's recent actions and statements "are intended to subvert and impair" contract negotiations.
US Airways, the nation's sixth largest airline, has been in labour talks with its pilots since their contract became amendable in April 1996.

The lawsuit, which was filed in federal district court in Pittsburgh, seeks injunctive relief against "further improper conduct," as well as damages under the Railway Labour Act, the federal statute that governs the airline industry's labour relations.
US Airways called the lawsuit "frivolous."

"It appears that things are coming to a head. The airline clearly has to make a decision sooner rather than later on what they will do," said Susan Donofrio, an airline analyst with NatWest Securities Corp.

The issue of growth, as well as compensation, job security and the development of a low-cost "response" to compete with carriers such as Southwest Airlines Co., has been a key stumbling point in negotiations.
From 1990 through 1996, US Airways has shrunk an average of three percent a year, while its major competitors have grown an average of 3.6 percent a year, the company said.

US Airways had previously said it was at a "crossroads." If the company did not reach a cost-cutting pact with its unionized employees, it would be forced to become a smaller, regional carrier, the company told shareholders at its annual meeting in May.
But with an agreement, the company could expand by adding flights and building up its international operations.

In recent months, US Airways has laid off pilots and threatened additional layoffs, base closings, downsizing and cancellation of an order for 400 aircraft unless it was able to cut costs. The airline plans to cancel the jet order if it does not have a competitive cost structure in place by September.

US Airways, which has among the highest costs in the airline industry, needs up to $1.5 billion in wage, salary and productivity concessions to bring its costs in line with the rest of the industry, analysts said.
US Airways made similar comments about needing to downsize unless it slashed costs in a series of letters and a videotape sent to pilots' homes, the pilots union said said.
The union said the company's comments allegedly violated the federal law, which requires management to deal with the union leaders and not negotiate directly with or threaten the pilots.
The two sides continued negotiations on Thursday, with the union calling the company's growth offer a "break in the road block."

"Management had stonewalled on the issue of growth, stonewalled on compensation and stonewalled on job security. Maybe this is an indication that ... the block has broken," said Jim Gardner, a spokesman for the pilots union.
"But the devil is in the details and there are a lot of details," Gardner said.

In addition to the growth proposal, the airline also reiterated its offer to give the pilots a "contractual guarantee that will give them compensation parity with our major competitors -- American, Delta, Northwest and United."
